scope: Private immutable recorded image-verification observation and typed support artifact under DE-W034. Preserve the original AcquisitionCase; no new product command, stable persisted/public ABI, authenticated custody or present-day storage authority.
binding: Construct from an exact typed acquisition case, the actual bounded raw request bytes, the prepared verification definition, typed outcome and separately supplied observation context. Validate the source descriptor, exact case revision/store, raw request length/hash and parsed header equality, recorded history length/hash, and original plan equality. Bind verifier code identity, wall/elapsed clock observations, case before/after and image/map before/after bindings. Native image/map bindings must reproduce the prepared read-resource identities, epochs, original generation epochs and sizes. No retained path is followed by this pure model. This ordinary-Windows-binding prototype admits verifier target_profile=windows.nt10.x64.win32 only; source_state is clean, dirty or exported, source revision is exact lowercase Git SHA-1 and code digests are exact lowercase SHA-256. Do not forward arbitrary text as a target identity. Other-platform code/bindings require their own implemented qualification.
outcome: Reprepare the definition and enforce its complete value/digest, known outcome/revalidation states, coverage=matched prefix, bounded record/map counts, source/substitution partition without overflow and read>=matched. Accepted records require at least their nonempty body/LF byte accounting; no matched/read/record prefix exists without a before-resource observation. Sealed requires full coverage and no pending range. Matched additionally requires full canonical map byte accounting, exact image size, a seal, no diagnostic and unchanged before/after verification resources. Passed revalidation requires both resource snapshots equal the definition; changed/unavailable stays unknown; not_attempted has no observations/counters. Invalid relationships refuse receipt construction rather than asserting success.
applicability: Case and late image-binding revalidation each say passed, changed or unavailable. Passed requires identical validated before/after bindings; changed requires a different validated after binding; unavailable requires null after. Derive attachment_applicability conservatively: unavailable dominates changed, then applicable. Preserve an independently matched verification outcome even when a later case/image binding invalidates attachment. Historical applicable is an observation at capture time, not permission or a claim about the latest files.
clock: domain is windows-filetime-wall with positive canonical u64 started/finished and observed monotonic elapsed_ms, or unobserved with three null values. Derive wall_clock_regressed from the wall values; do not derive elapsed time or causal order from an adjustable wall clock. A clock or code declaration authenticates no observer.
immutability: Retain deep immutable snapshots and SHA-256 of the entire bounded canonical private view as its revision. Original case support retains current_image_verification=not_performed. This separate record does not rewrite earlier evidence, restart workers or repair files. Retention and permission to execute remain separate.
disclosure: Exactly four policy booleans: identifiers, raw_values, interpretations, customer_data. Default support includes recorded status, verification resource revalidation, separate case/image-binding revalidation, attachment applicability, seal/pending markers and fixed claim limitations. raw_values adds only seven counters and clock. identifiers adds only case/operation/attempt/worker IDs and actual verifier code identity. interpretations adds a labeled inference about the recorded matching observation being bound to the case, never latest-image or source-preservation success. customer_data selects no further fields for this artifact. Never disclose original case/request/history/definition/resource/observation digests, routing paths, arbitrary diagnostics, private bindings or hashes/pseudonyms of omitted customer data under any policy.
artifact: SupportArtifact accepts the typed immutable observation, encodes compact sorted JSON UTF-8 plus one LF, and uses scope recorded-image-verification-support. Its digest covers selected output bytes only. The existing ordinary-file export adapter may qualify this private artifact using explicit effect-definition digest, report_write and host_effects grants. Preparation creates no output. Keep source revalidation, actual output facts and export uncertainty separate; preserve partial outputs and do not retry automatically. Current product acquisition-report/export schemas continue to reject this new private scope until their own admission contracts are extended. The native qualification probe reviews a private wrapper containing exact observation and case revisions, case/image source bindings and the complete effect definition. Its three-field effect grant uses that wrapper digest; an inner-only or wrong digest cannot execute. Per-step held-source checks guard the actual ordinary-file adapter. The inner output receipt retains its own effect digest. This private probe wrapper is not a stable product worker/store command contract.
qualification: Independently check canonical full-view revision, immutable snapshots, wrong case/plan/request/history/binding/code/clock/outcome relationships, all 16 exact support projections and artifact bytes/digests. Use actual generated acquisition verification, real byte and metadata changes, and actual explicitly granted ordinary-file support exports. Keep synthetic receipt alterations separate; preserve unfinished/failed dependencies and the prior acquisition case bytes/claims.
next_gate: Qualify durable observation/custody collections, bounded same-file reader worker/store/watch/cancellation and actual product frontend journeys before image.verify availability. Authenticated actors, all specified storage/platforms and owner/physical/elevation/customer/install/signing/publication/release gates remain separate.
